subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Commands are built-in instructions for computer programs.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Built-in instructions for the same type of data differ among programming languages.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: In Python, the command "S-T-R" means "string," representing characters and letters.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Syntax, static semantics, and semantics define a programming language.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Syntax tells us the sequence of characters and symbols allowed in the programming language's rules.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Syntax in computer programming is like syntax in human languages.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Syntax does not care if something has meaning, only that it fits the programming language's rules.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Static semantics refer to how meaningful and well-formed a code is.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Programming languages, unlike human languages, have only one meaning.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: A bug is an error in the code that goes against the intention of the coder.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Errors can cause the program to quit, resulting in a crash.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Errors can also cause the program to become unresponsive, resulting in a freeze.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Crashing and freezing have different underlying causes.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: Incompatibility, when a program expects one input but gets another, can cause a crash.

subject: ComputerScience
sentence: When a program gets stuck in an infinite loop and cannot complete a job, it can cause a freeze.
